title: Standings source-dedup only guards the 2003-2019 Brasileirão window
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp.py:213 restricts single-source aggregation to `2003 <= season <= 2019`; for other seasons standings aggregate every match whose competition contains the query string, so overlapping datasets could double-count if a second file labels the same competition.
suggestion: Deduplicate matches by (date, home, away) before tabulating standings, or extend the single-source rule to all seasons.

title: head_to_head embeds full match dicts in every response
evidence: brazilian_soccer_mcp.py:201 sets `matches_data`: [asdict(m) for m in matches] with no limit, so a high-volume pairing returns a large payload alongside the summary counts.
suggestion: Cap or paginate matches_data, or make the full match list opt-in.

title: MCP JSON-RPC serve loop is untested
evidence: test_brazilian_soccer_mcp.py exercises the SoccerData service directly; serve()/call_tool() (brazilian_soccer_mcp.py:263-288) have no test, consistent with test_coverage=0.85 (not 1.0).
suggestion: Add a test that drives serve() with an initialize + tools/call line to cover the protocol layer.
